keySentence: Passepartout showed that loyalty is worth more than money.

facts.Page story text 1 (draft, teacher check: Fogg thanked Passepartout silently. Good friends respect each other. Loyalty goes both ways. Passepartout showed that loyalty is worth more than money.
facts.Page story text 2 (draft, teacher check: As the journey continued, Fogg quietly appreciated Passepartout more and more. True loyalty is not one-sided — it must go both ways. Fogg respected Passepartout as a true companion, not just a servant. Their bond grew stronger with each challenge they overcame together. Passepartout showed that loyalty is worth more than money. When people truly respect each other, they can overcome anything.
facts.Page story text 3 (draft, teacher check: Throughout their incredible journey, the relationship between Fogg and Passepartout evolved beautifully. What began as a formal employer-servant arrangement grew into a genuine partnership of mutual respect. Fogg, though rarely showing emotion, demonstrated his appreciation through small but meaningful gestures. He treated Passepartout not as a subordinate but as a valued companion and equal. Passepartout showed that loyalty is worth more than money. However, true loyalty cannot exist without mutual respect and genuine caring from both sides. Because both men proved their dedication through actions rather than words, their bond became unbreakable. Together, they showed that the strongest partnerships are built on loyalty, respect, and shared purpose.
